history.summary: Shiva temple on the banks of the Mahanadi at Rudri, a small town near Dhamtari, beside the Rudri pick-up weir (Rudri Dam, built 1912–15). The sanctum houses a Swayambhu (self-manifested) Shiva Lingam; a tourism site notes shrines of the 12 Jyotirlingas and an Akhand Jyoti in the complex. Local legend (Sthalapurana) says Rama, Sita and Lakshmana stopped here to worship Shiva during the Vanavasa, making it part of the Ram Van Gaman Path; the temple was reportedly in dilapidated condition and has been renovated in the last ~10 years. A fair is organised in Shravan, at Shivratri and at Maghi Purnima, with jalabhishek crowds from 3–4 am. Coordinates below are approximate (from the Rudreshwar Mahadev Ghat listing; the exact temple pin is unverified).

name: Rudreshwar Mahadev Temple, Rudri
town_description: Rudri is a small town in Dhamtari district, Chhattisgarh, on the Mahanadi river, about 7 km from Dhamtari city. It is known for the Rudri pick-up weir (built 1912–15, once generating 0.2 MW of electricity), from which irrigation canals were taken in the early 20th century — the 1920 canal satyagraha that brought Mahatma Gandhi to Dhamtari was rooted in this project. The Rudreshwar Mahadev temple on the riverbank makes it a local pilgrimage and picnic spot.

travel.road: Near the Rudri Dam/pick-up weir, ~7 km from Dhamtari town by road (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; Shravan and Mahashivaratri for the major fairs
